brief.title: A3 poster: Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic
brief.brief:
Design an A3 portrait poster (297 x 420 mm) for the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic, run by Spoke & Chain, a neighborhood bike repair shop. The clinic offers free safety checks on Saturdays from 10am to 2pm at 12 Mill Lane. Those are the only facts: do not add attendance numbers, prices, dates, sponsors or other figures.

Deliver the poster as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the poster as a fluid layout that fits a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: A3 portrait; margin: 0 } (297 x 420 mm) so it prints as exactly one A3 page with the artwork filling the page and nothing else printed.

requirements.description: A clear, prominent headline naming the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic.
States that safety checks are free and that the clinic runs Saturday 10am to 2pm.
Shows the address line "12 Mill Lane".
Contains no invented attendance numbers, statistics, prices or other facts beyond the brief.

judge.reason: The poster meets all four requirements, with the clinic name, free checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm and 12 Mill Lane all shown and no invented facts.

checks.reason: The desktop and phone screenshots show a large serif h1 reading "Saturday Fix-It & Clinic" with "Spoke & Chain" in the masthead and kicker, so the clinic is named prominently.
The page states "Free safety checks" in the slot and "Saturday, 10am to 2pm" in the When slot, with the body repeating both facts.
The footer shows "12 Mill Lane" as a large address line, and the body copy also includes it.
The copy uses only the supplied facts (free safety checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm, 12 Mill Lane); no attendance numbers, prices or statistics appear.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, editorial poster with a large serif headline, a wheel illustration and a What/When slot that makes the offer easy to scan. The brief's facts are all present and nothing is invented.
strengths: Large serif headline "Saturday Fix-It & Clinic" with the accent-coloured ampersand dominates the top of the page.
The What/When slot states "Free safety checks" and "Saturday, 10am to 2pm" side by side.
The wheel line illustration in the brand accent colour gives the poster a clear bike theme.
weaknesses: The phone layout stacks the wheel illustration over the deck text, so the deck's words cross the spokes and are harder to read.
The body copy repeats the same facts as the slot and footer, which adds clutter without new information.
The phone screenshot is cramped toward the bottom, with the body text running close to the footer rule.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a plain, text-led poster with a strong headline and no extra imagery beyond the bike wheel.

checks.reason: The h1 reads "Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic" in large bold type at the top of the sheet, visible in both the desktop and phone screenshots.

The markup includes "Free safety checks" and a "Saturday, 10am to 2pm" card, but the sheet has a fixed aspect ratio with overflow:hidden. On desktop only the start of the Admission card is visible, and the hours card is cut off. On the phone only the Admission heading shows, so the Saturday 10am to 2pm offer is not visible to a viewer.

"12 Mill Lane" appears only in the Where card and the footer. Both are clipped below the bottom edge of the sheet in the desktop and phone screenshots, so the address is not visible on the page as a viewer sees it.
The copy uses only the supplied facts: free safety check, Saturdays 10am to 2pm, 12 Mill Lane, and the neighborhood repair shop. It contains no attendance numbers, prices or statistics.

judge.reason: The poster meets the content requirements on desktop, but on a phone the fixed-ratio container clips the bottom of the poster so the when/where details are cut off.

checks.reason: The h1 reads Spoke & Chain / Saturday / Fix-It Clinic in large white and orange type at the top of the desktop poster, and the same headline shows on the 390px phone view.

Desktop shows FREE SAFETY CHECKS in the orange panel and SATURDAYS 10am to 2pm under WHEN. On the phone first view the poster is clipped by overflow:hidden, so the 10am to 2pm line is cut off and not visible there, though it is in the page markup.
Desktop shows 12 MILL LANE under WHERE, and the footer also contains 12 Mill Lane. On the phone first view the address is cut off mid-line, so it is only fully visible on desktop.

The copy uses only the brief's facts (free safety checks, Saturdays 10am to 2pm, 12 Mill Lane, neighborhood bike repair shop) with no figures, prices or statistics. The phrase 'our mechanics will look over your bike' is a mild embellishment but not a factual claim.

narrative.overall_verdict: A bold, high-contrast black and orange poster with a clear headline and a prominent FREE SAFETY CHECKS panel that serves the brief well on desktop. On a 390px phone the fixed-ratio box cuts off the WHEN/WHERE details and footer on first load, so the time and address are not visible without scrolling inside the artwork.
strengths: Large split headline (Spoke & Chain / Saturday / Fix-It Clinic) gives a clear, prominent title.
The orange FREE SAFETY CHECKS block stands out strongly against the black background.
Copy sticks to the brief's facts with no invented numbers, prices or statistics.
weaknesses: On a 390px phone the poster is clipped at the bottom, hiding the 10am to 2pm time and most of the 12 Mill Lane address on first load.
The decorative wheel runs behind the headline and the word CLINIC, reducing legibility at the edge of the title.
The description 'Our mechanics will look over your bike' adds a service claim the brief did not supply, which the buyer should verify.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a bold, high-contrast poster that reads well on desktop and print.
